notes: All endpoints are same-origin and authenticated via the SSO session cookie. The extension calls them with default browser credentials; we never read, store, or transmit auth headers.

main_init.purpose: PRIMARY: Returns store config + the entire scheduled associates roster + schedule changes + headcount changes for a given store and business date.
main_init.bodyShape: unknown (XHR observed as POST with query params; body content not captured)

responseShape.wm_yr_wk: object with wm_yr, wm_wk, wk_start_date, wk_end_date, ly_comp_yr, ly_comp_wk

schedule.scheduled_associates: Array<object>(per-associate; field names PENDING schema dump)

responseShape.schedule_changes: Array<object>(empty in test run; likely call-in/call-off entries)

main_init.triggeredBy: search.submitButton click; also fires on page load when defaults are set
main_init.source: recon artifact 2026-05-22 — XHR at 9545ms returned 200 in 2065ms
main_init.notes: This is the canonical source for the closing list. Per-associate field names within scheduled_associates need a schema dump (see recon-helper/inspect-associate-schema.js).

pallet_pickup_planned.purpose: Planned pallet pickup info per store. Not needed for closing email.

shipments_load_summary.purpose: Per-load shipment details. Not needed for closing email.
shipments_load_summary.responseShape: {status, message, store_nbr, load_id, shipment_type, data_source, refreshed_from_api, shipment_summary[], shipment_details[]}
shipments_load_summary.source: recon XHRs at 11607-11608ms (multiple parallel calls per shipment)

star_freight.purpose: Star freight events from DB2. Not needed for closing email.
star_freight.notes: Out of scope for ClosingList. Large response.

hit_counter.purpose: Page logs usage analytics back to the server.
hit_counter.notes: Do NOT call from the extension. We are not the page; we should not poison usage analytics with synthetic hits. The page itself will log when the user opens it normally.

csrfTokenSource.purpose: Check whether any anti-forgery token is required.
csrfTokenSource.source: recon — no CSRF token query params or headers observed on any XHR
csrfTokenSource.notes: Cookie-only auth appears sufficient. If a token does exist, it would be in a header we deliberately didn't capture — but the pattern of these ASHX endpoints suggests classic ASP.NET handlers without anti-forgery middleware.
